title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
why_read: An interesting approach where a simulation generator and a robot policy improve each other in a loop, systematically targeting the policy's actual weaknesses.
analysis: CoDA pairs a simulated-environment generator with a robot action policy, using a shared memory of past failures and a vision-language model critic to decide what new training scenarios would actually help the policy improve. It converts diagnosed failure patterns into dense reward-like signals through a method called Text2potential, which gives the policy more informative feedback than just success or failure. The reported jumps in out-of-distribution success rates, going from single digits to double digits or more, are notable if they hold up outside the paper's specific benchmarks. This is a reasonably novel systems-level idea for automating curriculum design in robot learning rather than hand-crafting training scenarios.
